title: Samaria
lead: The capital of the northern kingdom, built by Omri on a hill he bought (1 Kings 16:24), and later the name of the whole region between Judea and Galilee. It fell to Assyria in 722 BC; Herod rebuilt it as Sebaste, and in Acts Philip preached there.

sections.b: Omri bought the hill from Shemer for two talents of silver and built his capital there (1 Kings 16:24). Ahab built a temple of Baal and an ivory house in it (1 Kings 16:32; 1 Kings 22:39), and the prophets attacked the luxury of its leaders (Amos 3:15; Amos 4:1; Amos 6:1). Assyria besieged it for three years and took it in 722 BC, deporting its people and settling others in the land (2 Kings 17:5–6, 24). Excavations have uncovered a royal compound with fine masonry and hundreds of carved ivories. In the New Testament the region of Samaria lies between Judea and Galilee (John 4:4), and Philip preached in "the city of Samaria" (Acts 8:5).
